meta.mechanism: PCSK9 inhibitor (fully human monoclonal antibody); increases hepatic LDL receptor recycling, lowers LDL-C ~60%
meta.modality: monoclonal antibody (subcutaneous, 140 mg Q2W or 420 mg monthly)
meta.indication: secondary prevention of major adverse cardiovascular events in stable atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (prior MI, ischemic stroke or symptomatic PAD) on statin therapy

n_randomized.quote: From February 2013 through June 2015, a total of 27,564 patients underwent randomization to either the evolocumab group (13,784 patients) or the placebo group (13,780 patients)

median_followup.quote: The median duration of follow-up was 26 months (interquartile range, 22 to 30), which resulted in 59,865 patient-years of follow-up.
median_followup.note: Abstract states 2.2 years. Discussion: follow-up was originally planned at ~4 years but an event rate ~50% higher than postulated shortened it.

primary_endpoint.value: Composite of cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, stroke, hospitalization for unstable angina, or coronary revascularization (key secondary: CV death, MI, or stroke)
primary_endpoint.quote: The primary efficacy end point was the composite of cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, stroke, hospitalization for unstable angina, or coronary revascularization. The key secondary efficacy end point was the composite of cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, or stroke.

inclusion_key_criteria.value: Age 40-85; clinically evident ASCVD (prior MI, nonhemorrhagic stroke or symptomatic PAD); fasting LDL-C >=70 mg/dL or non-HDL-C >=100 mg/dL on optimized statin; TG <=400 mg/dL
inclusion_key_criteria.quote: The study population consists of 27,564 patients who have had a myocardial infarction (MI), an ischemic stroke, or symptomatic peripheral artery disease and have a low-density lipoprotein ≥70 mg/dL or a non-high-density lipoprotein cholesterol ≥100 mg/dL on an optimized statin regimen.
inclusion_key_criteria.note: Age and TG limits from registry S3 eligibility: 'Male or female ≥ 40 to ≤ 85 years of age' and 'Fasting triglycerides ≤ 400 mg/dL (4.5 mmol/L)'.

planned_events.unit: events (key secondary end point: CV death, MI, stroke)
planned_events.quote: The size of the patient population in the trial was based on the key secondary end point, and we estimated that 1630 such end-point events were required to provide 90% power to detect a 15% relative risk reduction with evolocumab as compared with placebo.
planned_events.note: Sizing based on the key secondary end point, not the primary. Also in design paper S4 abstract (pub 2015-12-17) and Amgen press release S2.

assumed_rrr.quote: 1630 such end-point events were required to provide 90% power to detect a 15% relative risk reduction with evolocumab as compared with placebo.
assumed_rrr.note: Applies to key secondary end point. Design paper S4: 'relative reduction of ≥15%'.

power.quote: 1630 such end-point events were required to provide 90% power

alpha.quote: If the rate of the primary end point was significantly lower in the evolocumab group (P<0.05), then, in a hierarchical fashion, the key secondary end point and then cardiovascular death were to be tested at a significance level of 0.05.
alpha.note: Sidedness not stated explicitly in main text; registry S3 also says 'significance level of 0.05'. Two-sided assumed (log-rank, conventional); see open_questions.

stopped_early.quote: Although the median follow-up period in FOURIER was originally planned to be approximately 4 years, an event rate that was approximately 50% higher than had been postulated led to a shorter required duration of follow-up to accrue the prespecified number of events.
stopped_early.note: Not stopped early for efficacy/harm; ended on reaching planned events, earlier than planned calendar time because event rate was higher than postulated.

baseline.quote: The median LDL cholesterol level at baseline was 92 mg per deciliter (interquartile range, 80 to 109) (2.4 mmol per liter [interquartile range, 2.1 to 2.8]).
baseline.note: 2.4 mmol/L. Friedewald LDL-C (see method in biomarker_effects).
IQR 13-166 evolocumab, 13-164 placebo. O'Donoghue S5 (Lp(a) measured in 25,096 patients): 'The median (interquartile range) baseline Lp(a) concentration was 37 (13-165) nmol/L.'
NOT FOUND: baseline apoB not reported in main-text Table 1 (likely in Supplementary Appendix, not accessed).
NOT FOUND in main text. Table 1 gives TC 168 and HDL-C 44 mg/dL medians (difference of medians is not the median non-HDL-C).

biomarker_effects.method: Friedewald calculated LDL-C; preparative ultracentrifugation when Friedewald LDL-C <40 mg/dL (per S6)
biomarker_effects.quote: At 48 weeks, the least-squares mean percentage reduction in LDL cholesterol levels with evolocumab, as compared with placebo, was 59% (95% confidence interval [CI], 58 to 60; P<0.001), for a mean absolute reduction of 56 mg per deciliter (95% CI, 55 to 57) (1.45 mmol per liter [95% CI, 1.43 to 1.47]), to a median of 30 mg per deciliter
biomarker_effects.note: Absolute = -1.45 mmol/L (95% CI 1.43-1.47). Fig. 1 absolute differences over time range 50-58 mg/dL (54% to 61%), i.e. effect maintained. Method from S6 (PMC open): 'Preparative ultracentrifugation LDL-C ascertainment was performed when the Friedewald LDL-C level was less than 40 mg/dL'. CTT check (derived, not from source): 0.78^1.45 = 0.70 expected RR over ~5 years vs observed HR 0.85 primary / 0.80 key secondary at median 2.2 y; key-secondary RRR beyond year 1 was 25% (S1: 'from 16% (95% CI, 4 to 26) in the first year to 25% (95% CI, 15 to 34) beyond the first year').

biomarker_effects.method: Friedewald calculated LDL-C; preparative ultracentrifugation when <40 mg/dL
biomarker_effects.quote: for a mean absolute reduction of 56 mg per deciliter (95% CI, 55 to 57) (1.45 mmol per liter [95% CI, 1.43 to 1.47])
biomarker_effects.note: Same measurement as above, in mmol/L.

biomarker_effects.quote: as compared with placebo, at 48 weeks, evolocumab had reduced non-HDL cholesterol levels by 52% and apolipoprotein B levels by 49% (P<0.001 for both).
biomarker_effects.note: Absolute non-HDL-C change NOT FOUND (Fig. S3 of supplement not accessed).

biomarker_effects.method: central lab immunoassay (assay not specified in main text)
biomarker_effects.quote: as compared with placebo, at 48 weeks, evolocumab had reduced non-HDL cholesterol levels by 52% and apolipoprotein B levels by 49% (P<0.001 for both).
At 48 weeks, evolocumab significantly reduced Lp(a) by a median (interquartile range) of 26.9% (6.2%-46.7%).
biomarker_effects.note: Read in abstract only (Circulation, subscription per Europe PMC). Whether 26.9% is placebo-adjusted is not stated in the abstract; reported as 'evolocumab significantly reduced'. Median, not mean.

biomarker_effects.quote: At the end of the dosing interval at week 12, the mean LDL-C concentrations were reduced generally dose dependently by AMG 145 every 2 weeks (ranging from 41·8% to 66·1%; p<0·0001 for each dose vs placebo) and AMG 145 every 4 weeks (ranging from 41·8% to 50·3%; p<0·0001).
biomarker_effects.note: Phase 2 dose-ranging on statin background, n=631; published online 2012-11-06, before readout. Upper end of range (140 mg Q2W) shown; range 41.8-66.1% Q2W. Whether figures are placebo-subtracted is not explicit in the abstract (placebo_adjusted=null).

biomarker_effects.quote: As compared with standard therapy alone, evolocumab reduced the level of LDL cholesterol by 61%, from a median of 120 mg per deciliter to 48 mg per deciliter (P<0.001).
biomarker_effects.note: Open-label extension of phase 2/3 parent trials (n=4465), control = standard therapy (not placebo). Absolute -72 mg/dL is derived (120-48 medians), not reported as a difference. Exploratory CV events HR 0.47 (0.28-0.78). Published 2015-03-15, before readout.

hr.quote: evolocumab treatment significantly reduced the risk of the primary end point (1344 patients [9.8%] vs. 1563 patients [11.3%]; hazard ratio, 0.85; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.79 to 0.92; P<0.001)
hr.note: Key secondary (CV death/MI/stroke): 816 [5.9%] vs 1013 [7.4%]; HR 0.80 (0.73-0.88), P<0.001. CV death HR 1.05 (0.88-1.25); all-cause death HR 1.04 (0.91-1.19); MI HR 0.73 (0.65-0.82) (Table 2). Registry S3 reports identical HR 0.85 (0.79-0.92), p<0.0001.

p.quote: hazard ratio, 0.85; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.79 to 0.92; P<0.001

safety_signals.value: Injection-site reactions more frequent with evolocumab: 296 (2.1%) vs 219 (1.6%)
safety_signals.quote: Injection-site reactions were rare, but they were more frequent with evolocumab (2.1% vs. 1.6%).

safety_signals.value: No excess new-onset diabetes: HR 1.05 (0.94-1.17); 677 (8.1%) vs 644 (7.7%)
safety_signals.quote: The rates of adjudicated cases of new-onset diabetes did not differ significantly between the two groups (hazard ratio, 1.05; 95% CI, 0.94 to 1.17).
Likewise, the rates of muscle-related events, cataract, neurocognitive adverse events, and hemorrhagic stroke did not differ significantly between the two groups.
safety_signals.note: EBBINGHAUS cognitive substudy met non-inferiority per Amgen press release S2 (not separately verified here).

safety_signals.value: Antidrug antibodies rare: binding antibodies 43 patients (0.3%), no neutralizing antibodies
safety_signals.quote: In the evolocumab group, new binding antibodies developed in 43 patients (0.3%), and development of neutralizing antibodies did not occur in any patient.
safety_signals.note: Contrast with bococizumab (humanized) attenuation noted in Discussion.

genetics.finding: PCSK9 nonsense (loss-of-function) mutations in ARIC black participants associated with 28% lower LDL-C and 88% lower CHD risk; R46L in whites 15% lower LDL-C and 47% lower CHD risk
genetics.effect: HR 0.11 (0.02-0.81) blacks; HR 0.50 (0.32-0.79) whites over 15 years
genetics.quote: Of the 3363 black subjects examined, 2.6 percent had nonsense mutations in PCSK9; these mutations were associated with a 28 percent reduction in mean LDL cholesterol and an 88 percent reduction in the risk of CHD

genetics.finding: PCSK9 nonsense mutations Y142X and C679X common in African Americans and associated with ~40% lower LDL-C
genetics.quote: These mutations were common in African Americans (combined frequency, 2%) but rare in European Americans (<0.1%) and were associated with a 40% reduction in plasma levels of LDL cholesterol.

genetics.finding: Mendelian randomization: PCSK9 and HMGCR variants give near-identical CV protection per unit LDL-C lowering
genetics.effect: OR 0.81 (0.74-0.89) per 10 mg/dL lower LDL-C for PCSK9 score
genetics.quote: Variants in PCSK9 and HMGCR were associated with nearly identical protective effects on the risk of cardiovascular events per decrease of 10 mg per deciliter (0.26 mmol per liter) in the LDL cholesterol level: odds ratio for cardiovascular events, 0.81 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.74 to 0.89) for PCSK9

genetics.finding: LDL-C is causal; CTT meta-analysis: major vascular events reduced ~22% per 1 mmol/L LDL-C reduction (benchmark for calculator)
genetics.quote: similar proportional reductions in major vascular events per 1·0 mmol/L LDL cholesterol reduction were found in all types of patient studied (rate ratio [RR] 0·78, 95% CI 0·76-0·80; p<0·0001)

consensus_explanation.summary: Genetically validated target (PCSK9 loss-of-function protects against CHD) and a large, durable, placebo-adjusted LDL-C reduction (59%, 1.45 mmol/L, to median 30 mg/dL) with no attenuation (fully human antibody, no neutralizing antibodies). A large, well-powered event-driven trial (27,564 patients, 1630 planned key secondary events) in high-risk ASCVD. Benefit was modest in relative terms (15% primary, 20% key secondary) because median follow-up was only 2.2 years; benefit grew over time (key secondary RRR 16% year 1 to 25% beyond year 1), consistent with the CTT per-mmol/L relationship for MI, stroke and urgent revascularization. No CV-mortality effect within the short follow-up. Safety clean apart from injection-site reactions.

open_questions: Alpha sidedness: NEJM text says 'significance level of 0.05' without stating two-sided; recorded 0.05 two-sided as assumption.
Power calculation is on the key secondary end point (CV death/MI/stroke, 1630 events), not the primary end point; the primary end point had 1344+1563=2907 events.
Baseline apoB and non-HDL-C, and absolute apoB/non-HDL-C reductions: NOT FOUND (Supplementary Appendix Fig. S3 not accessed).
Lp(a) 26.9% median reduction (S5) read in abstract only; unclear whether placebo-adjusted; Lp(a) assay not captured.

CTT comparison caveat: FOURIER median follow-up 2.2 y vs ~5 y in CTT trials. Expected RR from 0.78^1.45 = 0.70 (derived) vs observed HR 0.85 (primary) / 0.80 (key secondary); year >1 key secondary RRR 25%. Endpoint definitions also differ from CTT 'major vascular events'. The authors say MI, stroke and urgent revascularization benefit is 'largely consistent' with statins per mmol/L (Fig. S6, not accessed).
NEJM full text was read from third-party copies of the publisher PDF (conference CDN and natap.org), since nejm.org blocked automated access.
